correctness.rationale: Trace and determinant characterize shifted closed two-by-two spectral margin. For a real rank-one correction the planar Pythagorean identity gives exact norm, trace and determinant; a strictly increasing determinant envelope on the trace-feasible interval proves global minimum and extremizers for every \(a>0\), \(\delta\geq0\) and \(b\geq0\), including the impossibility at b=0. Explicit matrices give boundary rank and eigenvalues, signed semidefinite corrections give exact finite overdamping interval, and one-parameter families prove strict-margin infima. Replayed exact-rational standalone checker reports CHECKS_PASSED 39823; its finite cases support but do not substitute for the analytic proof. No unproved algebraic lemma remains.

value.rationale: The exact two-dimensional benchmark supplies an intrinsic Frobenius cost for low-rank spectral assignment, sharply compares full-rank and rank-one costs, classifies global minimizers, explains defective nonnormal boundary behavior, and proves that passive rank-one damping works only for sufficiently fast rotation and can destabilize by overdamping. These are motivated structural and optimization facts for low-rank stability correction rather than arbitrary numerical slices. Scope is fixed to real planar rotation-dilation with freely oriented rank-one updates, not broader numerical robustness claims.
